experiment: Grader robustness: the same E08b answers scored by 5 graders
question: How much does a model's score depend on which grader scores it?
contaminated: deepseek-v4-pro graded deepseek answers (same family); treat v4pro scores for deepseek-* cells as biased.
unit: passes out of 12 runs per cell; null = not graded (glm cells were graded by 3 graders only)
summary_spread_note: spread_max_min uses every grader that scored the cell (5 for kimi and deepseek, 3 for glm), so it is not comparable across models. spread_common_3 uses only luna, gemini and v4pro, which scored every cell.
finding: On the three graders that scored every cell, spread was 5-7 points (of 12) for kimi, 6-7 for deepseek and 2-4 for glm. With all five graders it reached 6-9 for kimi and deepseek: kimi-low got 12/12 from gemini, 10/12 from step-5 and v4pro, 5/12 from luna and 4/12 from sonnet. kimi's apparent lead exists only under the lenient graders (gemini, step-5, v4pro). Single-grader 'A beats B' claims in this repo are therefore treated as indicative, and the bar is a majority of three graders from different families.
limitations: v4pro is not cross-family for deepseek cells
notes: Models were called through an OpenAI-compatible router; names and prices are as recorded at run time.
